summary: Phillip E. Bloom works in Sinology, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2013), supervised by Eugene Y. Wang, Yukio Lippit, and James Robson.
Phillip Zarrilli (1947–2020) was a scholar in Indology and other fields. He held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1979–1998) and the University of Exeter (~1998–2020).

Phra Brahmapundit (born 1955) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He became Buddhist Chief Abbot at Wat Prayurawongsawat (~1996) and Rector of Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1997–2018), serving also as President of the International Association of Buddhist Universities (~2007).

Phra Medhidhammaporn (born 1955) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Delhi in 1985 under the supervision of Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Phra Rajavaramuni works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned B.A. degrees from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University and Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University, later serving as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies and Deputy Vice Rector at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2012).

Phra Sigambhirayan specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University and Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where he held an appointment as Associate Professor (attested 2013).
Phramaha Niras Ruangsan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Sydney, supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan.
Phramaha Sakda Hemthep is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MPhil at Cardiff University in 2014 under the supervision of Max Deeg.
Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of Sydney under the supervision of Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle (attested 2009).
Phrapongsak K. is a Buddhist studies scholar who held research appointments at Ryukoku University and the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center in 2015.

Phuntsok Tashi works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff (born 1947) works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her degrees from Radcliffe College and Harvard University (~1969–1973), and held professorships at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Yale University (2004).

Pierce Salguero specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University, and became professor of Asian History and Health Humanities at Penn State Abington around 2010.

Pierre Bourdieu (1930–2002) was a philosopher and scholar. Educated at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Benveniste, he held academic posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lille University, EHESS, and the Collège de France (1981–2001).
Pierre Chantraine (1899–1974) was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and Joseph Vendryes (~1920–1927). He held a post at the University of Paris from around 1938 to 1969.

Pierre-Sylvain Filliozat (1936–2024) was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the EFEO (1963–1967), the Chair of Sanskrit at the EPHE (1967–2004), and EHESS (~1967–2005), and served as President of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (2010).
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen specializes in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He earned his PhD from Leiden University by 1991, where he also served as a research fellow (attested 1996).

Pieter Hendrik Pott (1918–1989) worked in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology/history. He was curator at the National Museum of Ethnology, Leiden (~1947–1965), and held a post at Leiden University (1973).

Pietro Merlo (1850–1888) studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia and Giovanni Maria Bertini (1867). He subsequently taught and held professorships at the University of Pavia from 1877 until his death.

Piotr Balcerowicz (born 1964) specializes in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Warsaw, Banaras Hindu University, Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences, he held professorships at the University of Warsaw (~2000, 2011) and SWPS University (2008–2011).
